entities.summary: Grigor Stavrev Parlichev, also known as Grigorios Stavridis, was a Bulgarian writer, teacher and translator. He received acclaim as a "second Homer" in Greece for his poem O Armatolos. Afterwards, he became a Bulgarian national activist. Parlichev was subject to criticism by contemporary Bulgarian figures for what they regarded as poor knowledge of Bulgarian. His other notable works include the poems Skenderbeg, 1762 leto, and his autobiographical work Autobiography. In North Macedonia and Bulgaria, he is regarded as a pioneer of national awakening, but his national identity has been also disputed between both countries.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Grigor Parlichev's poem O Armatolos earned him acclaim as a 'second Homer' in Greece, while his works on Bulgarian national identity have been recognized as pioneering efforts in both North Macedonia and Bulgaria. His impact on the regional literary scene is notable but limited in scope.
